# dsh-plugin-updates
An update checker that only offers plugin releases your running DSH core can actually load.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Screenshot from a demo DSH instance with sample data.
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) web-profile plugin that tells you which of your installed plugins have a ne
wer release **that your running DSH can actually take**. It only notifies. It never installs, never
edits your profile, never runs a child process.
> **npm name.** The bare name `dsh-plugin-updates` is already taken on npm by an unrelated data pack
age, so this plugin is published as `@lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates`. The loader row id stays `plug
in-updates` either way.
## Why
Updating DSH plugins blind is risky. Two things go wrong in practice:
1. **Name collisions.** Many local plugins are `link:` folders or GitHub installs whose names also e
xist on npm as unrelated projects. A checker that looks packages up by name reports false "updates"
and, if you approve, installs somebody else's package. This plugin classifies every dependency by it

s **specifier** (`^1.2.0`, `link:`, `github:`, a release tarball URL), never by its bare name.
2. **
Wrong-core builds.** The newest release of a plugin often needs a newer DSH core than the one you ru
n. Installing it can blank the whole web UI. This plugin applies the same compatibility rule as the
DSH 0.2.1 loader against the **running** core version, so a 0.2.x-only build is never offered to a 0
loader against the **running** core version, so a 0.2.x-only build is never offered to a 0.1.5 host.
It also keeps a list of holds (versions you know to avoid), per package notes, and gives you a memor
y-capped apply command to copy, because a bare `pnpm add` on a busy machine can exhaust memory.
## What you get
- An **Updates** tab in the sidebar (needs `dsh-better-sidebar`, optional) with a live count badge,
grouped results, links (npm, releases, changelog, compare), **Check now**, **Ignore this version**,

**Snooze** and **Copy command**.
- A **Settings** section for the options below.
- A read-only agent

tool `plugin_updates` (and `plugin_updates_doctor`).
- `GET /dsh-plugin-updates/api/doctor` and a b

undled doctor skill.
- Zero configuration: defaults work as installed.
## Install (DSH web profile)
Install from npm: `dsh plugin --profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates`, or from GitHub: `d
sh plugin --profile web add github:lucagiftzek/dsh-plugin-updates`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` lists it in `dsh.profile.bundles`. A local ch
eckout works too: clone it, run `npm install --omit=dev` in it, then `dsh plugin --profile web add l
ink:/absolute/path/to/dsh-plugin-updates`. Requires Node 22.5 or newer and DSH 0.1.5-rc.1 up to (not
including) 0.3.0. The browser half hot-reloads; only the server half needs the restart.
Kill switch without uninstalling: add `- id: plugin-updates` with `disabled: true` to the profile `c
ordis.patch.yml`, or set `DSH_PLUGIN_UPDATES_DISABLE=1`.
## Settings
Settings live in the `dsh-plugin-updates` namespace on DSH 0.1.5 (Settings page, stored in `settings
.yaml`) and in the `plugin-updates` row of the profile `cordis.patch.yml` on DSH 0.2.x (settings for
ms). The plugin imports an old `settings.yaml` section once.
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch. |
| `intervalHours` | `12` | Hours between automatic checks (m

inimum 1). |
[该节后续省略]
## How it decides compatibility
1. **Classify by specifier.** `registry` (semver range, tag, `npm:` alias) is checked on npm. `githu
b:` and `git+https://github.com/...` are checked against GitHub tags and the default branch HEAD, wi
th the pinned commit read from `pnpm-lock.yaml`. A `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/downl
oad/<tag>/<file>.tgz` URL is checked against GitHub releases. `link:`, `file:`, `workspace:` are loc
al: they are compared with an upstream only when the `upstream` map names them, or with their own gi
thub.com origin when `checkOwnRemotes` is on. Anything else (another git host, another tarball host)

is shown as `manual`.
2. **Gate against the running core.** For each candidate version: if its `eng
ines.dsh` is declared, that range decides alone; otherwise every `@deepseek-ai/dsh` and `@deepseek-a
i/dsh-*` peer range must match. Matching uses `semver.satisfies(running, range, { includePrerelease:
true })`, so `>=0.2.1` refuses an rc and `>=0.2.1-0` accepts it. The DSH 0.1.5 core has no gate of
its own, so there the result is "declared compatible", not "verified". Nested `dsh.engines.dsh` rang

es are shown as a hint only.
3. **Pick the newest stable version that passes the gate** and is not o
n a hold. A newer version that fails the gate is reported next to it ("0.28.2 needs a newer core"),

never offered.
4. **Status** per package: `up-to-date`, `update-compatible`, `update-needs-newer-cor
e`, `update-needs-older-core`, `no-declared-range` (the new version declares nothing, verify by hand
), `held`, `snoozed`, `ignored`, `unreachable`, `manual`, `local`, `unknown`. A failed lookup is `un

reachable`, never `up-to-date`.
5. **Caret traps.** If a fresh resolve of your declared range (`^0.7
.4`) would pick a version your core cannot take, the package is flagged so you do not run a bare `pn
pick a version your core cannot take, the package is flagged so you do not run a bare `pnpm update`.
The badge counts `update-compatible` only.
## Privacy
- Only two hosts are ever contacted: **registry.npmjs.org** and **api.github.com**. Redirects to any

other host are refused. `allowHosts` is an explicit opt-in that is empty by default.
- No telemetry

, no catalog download, no mirrors, no analytics.
- The only data sent is package names, versions and

repository names from your own profile, the same data `npm view` would send.
- Responses are cached
with ETags in `$DSH_HOME/dsh-plugin-updates/state.json` (mode 0600), never in the profile. Registry
and GitHub text is never shown or given to the model: only validated version strings and links the

plugin builds itself.
- Unauthenticated GitHub access allows 60 requests per hour. A sweep of a larg
e profile needs roughly 30 requests with ETags. The plugin stops below 10 remaining and reports the
rest as `unreachable` until the reset.
